title: Fukuyama Warns AI Could Reduce Us to His "Last Man"
source_used: Seoul Economic Daily (opinion column by Hong Byung-moon, AI-translated from Korean)
key_facts: Francis Fukuyama, author of The End of History and the Last Man, published his memoir In the Realm of the Last Man last month.
In an interview with The New York Times he said he had not anticipated that a wealthy real estate developer would be seized by a lust for political power.
He is concerned that the AI challenge to liberal democracy is not properly grasped, because many people watch AI with curiosity and accept it as progress.
The column cites 22 leading AI scholars, including Geoffrey Hinton, the Nobel physics laureate, who warned in a joint paper that humanity could lose control of AI.
The column argues that a global AI response body modelled on the International Atomic Energy Agency must be built faster.
The article is a commentary, and it says quotes from foreign sources are based on Korean-language reports and may not reflect exact wording.
quote_evidence: Fukuyama has recently been voicing concern over the challenge that artificial intelligence poses to the liberal democratic order.
There is no shortage of counterarguments holding that the case for AI regulation is a deliberate check by Big Tech firms seeking to block further entry into the AI market.
why_it_matters_hint: A columnist draws on Fukuyama's concern that AI may weaken liberal democracy and calls for an international AI body.
event_date: Column dated 8 Oct 2026; memoir published Sept 2026; the New York Times interview date not stated
notes: Opinion column (Commentary), not reporting: kept as analysis and labelled 'in a column'. Translated from Korean. Geoffrey Hinton's position is given as the article states it (Nobel physics laureate). Page carried sponsor offers, ignored.
